'''Kushida Shrine''' (櫛田宮, Kushida-gū) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|qid=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki City|1=Kanzaki, Saga}}, Saga Prefecture. It was formerly Ranked as a prefectural shrine. The famous {{ill|Kushida Shrine|en|Kushida Shrine|qid=Q865839|lt=Kushida Shrine (Fukuoka)|1=Kushida Shrine}} is its branch shrine.
== History ==
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō|1=Emperor Keikō}} when he traveled to the area. Hearing of local misfortunes, the emperor ordered the shrine built to enshrine a deity and bring peace to the land.<ref name="角川1">{{Cite book|editor=角川日本地名大辞典編纂委員会 |title=[[角川日本地名大辞典]] 41.佐賀県 |publisher=[[角川書店]] |year=1982 |isbn=978-4-04-622957-1 |ref=角川 }}</ref>
The name of the area, Kanzaki (神埼), is said to derive from the shrine's historical role in pacifying the region.<ref name="角川1" />
During the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|en|Mongol invasions of Japan|qid=Q208156|lt=Mongol invasions of Japan|1=Mongol invasions of Japan}}, the shrine's sacred sword was transferred to the Fukuoka Kushida Shrine, where prayers were conducted to repel the invaders.<ref name="角川1" /> Kushida Shrine in Fukuoka was later established as a branch of this shrine.
Kushida Shrine was one of three shrines revered as part of the {{ill|Kanzaki Manor|ja|神埼荘|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kanzaki Manor|qq=}}—along with {{ill|Koshi Shrine|ja|高志神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Oshitori Shrine|ja|白角折神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshitori Shrine|qq=}}—known collectively as the Three Great Shrines (三所大明神). These shrines continue to participate in the Miyuki Grand Festival, with mikoshi (portable shrines) from each joining the celebrations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kanzaki-museum.com/frmDataDetail.aspx?id=11570 |title=Miyuki Grand Festival |website=Kanzaki Digital Museum |publisher=Kanzaki City |accessdate=2024-03-02}}</ref>
The shrine saw significant renovations under the order of Emperor Toba in {{ill|1115 AD|ja|永久3年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1115 AD|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and was supported by influential local families.<ref name="角川1" /> It was designated as a Gōsha (village shrine) in 1871 and a Ken-sha (prefectural shrine) in 1880.<ref name="角川1" />
== Deities ==
Known collectively as "Kushida Sanshin":
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Kushinadahime|en|Kushinadahime|qid=Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushinadahime|1=Kushinadahime}}
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}}

* Kushimori Inari Shrine
* Kushimaru Inari Shrine
* Gion Shrine
* Benzaiten Shrine
* Tenmangu Shrine
== Festivals ==
* '''Spring Festival''' - Held annually on '''April 7–8'''
** Biennially celebrated as the '''Miyuki Grand Festival''' (on even-numbered years, the first weekend of April). Includes mikoshi processions and kagura (sacred music and dance) performances.
* '''Autumn Festival''' - Held annually on '''October 7–8'''
== Cultural Assets ==
=== Saga Prefecture Important Cultural Properties ===
* '''Hizen-style Stone Torii Gate''' - Built in {{ill|1602 AD|ja|慶長7年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1602 AD|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, features a distinctive design with three-part joints. Height: 3.35 m; crossbeam length: 4.45 m. Inscribed with the name of {{ill|Nabeshima Katsushige|en|Nabeshima Katsushige|qid=Q3138980|lt=Nabeshima Katsushige|1=Nabeshima Katsushige}}. Designated in 1964.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031433/index.html |title=Prefectural Cultural Properties (Structures) |publisher=Saga Prefecture |accessdate=2024-03-02}}</ref>
=== Important Folk Cultural Properties ===
* '''Goshinkō Festival Ema (votive tablet)''' - Large ema depicting the festival procession with mikoshi and lion dances. Dimensions: 159 cm × 184 cm. Dated to {{ill|1858 AD|ja|安政五年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1858 AD|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Designated in 1979.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031554/index.html |title=Prefectural Cultural Properties (Folk Materials) |publisher=Saga Prefecture |accessdate=2024-03-02}}</ref>
=== Significant Trees ===
* '''Koto no Kusu (Koto Camphor Tree)''' - A sacred camphor tree said to have grown from a koto buried by Emperor Keikō. Estimated age: 1,000 years. Circling the tree seven times is said to produce the sound of koto music.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kanzaki-museum.com/frmFeatureDetail.aspx?feature_id=4 |title=Kushida Shrine |website=Kanzaki Digital Museum |accessdate=2024-03-02}}</ref> Additional ancient trees include three camphors and one ginkgo over 700 years old.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji00369053/index.html |title=Saga Prefecture's Notable Trees |publisher=Saga Prefecture |accessdate=2023-08-10}}</ref>
== Access ==
* '''By Train:''' 10-minute walk southwest from {{ill|Kanzaki Station (Saga)|en|Kanzaki Station (Saga)|qid=Q5358654|lt=JR Kanzaki Station|1=Kanzaki Station (Saga)}} on the {{ill|Nagasaki Main Line|en|Nagasaki Main Line|qid=Q1078117|lt=Nagasaki Main Line|1=Nagasaki Main Line}}.
